newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria share index steady in brisk trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria share index steady in brisk trade.

text.p: The Nigerian stock exchange index closed little changed in brisk Monday trading.
The all-share index closed at 6,175.00 from 6,175.01 on Friday.
Many blue chips sectors rose, but a fall at Nigerian Breweries, one of the highest capitalised stocks on the market, swung the index back into the middle.
Unipetrol was 15 kobo up at 34.40 naira and African Petroleum added 14 kobo to 28.30 naira.
Construction firm G. Cappa closing up 24 kobo, the maximum five percent movement allowed daily, to 5.07 naira.
Benue Cement firmed to 4.00 naira, up 12 kobo. West African Portland Cement added 10 kobo to 28.12 naira, while Ashaka Cement rose five kobo to 15.05 naira.
Conglomerates PZ Industries and Lever Brothers appreciated by 10 kobo each to 32.80 naira and 24.40 naira respectively. However CFAO closed 10 kobo down at 5.70 naira.
Nigerian Breweries slid further, dropping 10 kobo to 13.60 naira, while International Breweries shed two kobo to 73 kobo.
Tyre makers Dunlop also dipped five kobo to 12.30 naira, with large volumes of shares on offer.

Among food shares, oil millers P.S. Mandrides rose five kobo to 2.20 naira. Flour Mills gained 10 kobo to 8.90 naira. Coca-Cola bottlers Nigerian Bottling Company closed five kobo higher at 26.30 naira.
Seven-Up Bottling Company fell to 2.10 naira, down three kobo.
Packaging shares remain depressed. Studio Press closing down five kobo at 1.25 naira.
Avon Crowncaps ended the day at 4.65 naira, losing three kobo, the same amount as Delta Glass which closed at 6.20 naira.
